# Accessibility conformance

<!-- Generated by `node tools/conformance.mjs --summary` from each component's `### Conformance (WCAG 2.2 AA)` table. Edit the tables, not this page. -->

For each component: the WCAG 2.2 level A and AA criteria it meets, how that was checked, and what the page author still owns. A team auditing to GIGW 3.0 can start here and follow the links to the table in each component's docs.

53 of 53 components have their conformance table written.

## What the statuses mean

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Meets | The component meets the criterion by itself, and a check in the repository shows it. |
| Meets with author's part | The component does its part and the criterion is met only when the page author does theirs (the label text, the heading, the language of a passage). The table row says what. |
| Not applicable | The criterion does not apply to this kind of component. The row says why. |
| Does not meet | A known gap. The row says what fails, measured, and the gap is listed below until it is fixed. |

A criterion is never listed as met without evidence: a check file in the repository, an axe run, a contrast test, or a manual test written down with what was done. The kinds of component and the criteria each must address are in `docs/contributing/conformance.md`.

## How the library tests

- **axe-core**, with the rules for WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 at levels A and AA, on component demos (`node tools/axe.mjs --url /packages/components/<name>/demo.html`; a table says when the check beside the component also runs it): in all three registers (quiet, warm, playful), in light and dark, at desktop width and at phone width (390 px, touch), and as a browser without JavaScript sees the page (`--no-js`). Components with a state that opens or changes (a menu with an order in progress, a dialog that is open) are also scanned in that state by their own check. axe finds roughly a third of WCAG problems; the rest is the checks below and the page author.
- **Component checks** (`npm run check`, one `*.check.mjs` per component): keyboard paths, focus, names and roles read from the browser's accessibility tree, live regions, target sizes, reflow at 390 px, and the page with JavaScript off. They run in Chromium, and in WebKit and Firefox with `--engine=` (see `docs/BROWSERS.md`). Screen reader behaviour is checked through the accessibility tree, not with a live screen reader.
- **Contrast**: every text role on every surface, in every palette and theme, is 4.5:1 or more (`packages/tokens/tokens.test.js`); components with drawn parts test those against 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), and some measure painted colours in the browser.
- **The touch check** (`node tools/touch.check.mjs`, part of `npm run check`): every interactive component answers a press within a frame, has a visible `:focus-visible` style, and keeps its colour change but drops movement under reduced motion, in all three registers (`docs/contributing/touch-contract.md`).
- **Forced colours and reduced motion**: checks emulate `forced-colors: active` and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` for the components that draw their own art. Reduced motion shows the finished still in every register. Forced colours brings back the browser's own control.

This is a statement of how the library is tested, not a certificate. A conformance claim covers a page, not a component, and the page author owns the parts below.

## Always the page author's

- Alt text for every image, and the text of every label, heading, link and error message the page writes.
- One page heading, a sensible heading order, a page title and the page's language (`lang` on `html`), and `lang` on any passage in another language (3.1.2).
- Skip links and landmarks for the page as a whole (2.4.1), and consistent navigation and help across pages (3.2.3, 3.2.4, 3.2.6).
- Captions, transcripts and audio description for any video or audio the page brings (1.2.x).
- The colours the page sets itself on top of the library's tokens, and the content a reader types or uploads.

## Known gaps

| Component | Criterion | What fails |
|---|---|---|
| [tooltip](../../packages/components/tooltip/tooltip.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | 1.4.13 Content on hover or focus | With JavaScript it meets all three parts. Dismissible: while the panel is open, Escape closes it wherever focus is, including with the pointer alone and no focus on the trigger, without moving focus (`packages/components/tooltip/tooltip.js`, a `keydown` listener on the document while open; `packages/components/tooltip/tooltip.check.mjs`: "<register>: pointer on the <trigger or panel>, no focus: Escape closes it and focus does not move", which failed on the trigger in all three registers before the fix, and passes in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox). Hoverable and persistent: the shown panel takes the pointer (`pointer-events: auto` while open), and the 8 px gap between trigger and panel belongs to the tooltip too, through two invisible bands as tall as the gap (`--sg-tooltip-gap`, 8 px) on the element itself, above and below the trigger (`sg-tooltip[data-open]::before` and `::after` in `packages/components/tooltip/tooltip.css`; they sit on the element, not the panel, because the panel's `overflow: auto` clipped a bridge drawn on it, and each band stops where the gap stops, so neither the trigger nor a button one gap away is covered: `tooltip.check.mjs`, "a click 1 px inside a button one gap below the trigger lands on that button", which failed with 12 px bands). Leaving the element (trigger, panel or bands) hides it after 300 ms. `tooltip.check.mjs`: "<register>: the point midway across the 8 px gap belongs to the tooltip (the panel or its bridge), not the page" (the element at that point was the page's `section` before the fix), "the pointer rests in the gap for 450 ms (longer than the 300 ms hide delay) and the tooltip is still open" (red with the bands removed), and "moving the pointer onto the panel keeps it open", in all three registers in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. Without JavaScript it does not meet the dismissible part: CSS alone reveals the panel on `:hover` and `:focus-within`, and CSS cannot answer a key, so Escape does nothing (manual test, 2026-10-07, JavaScript off: opacity 1 on hover and still 1 after Escape in a reviewer's probe on 7 October 2026). The no-JS reveal is hover and focus on the trigger, which the reader ends by moving away. |

| Component | The page author owns |
|---|---|
| [accordion](../../packages/components/accordion/accordion.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The question and answer text, in the language of the page.<br>`lang` on a question or answer in another language (3.1.2).<br>Alt text for images and the semantics of lists, links or headings put inside an answer.<br>Sticky headers or banners that could cover a summary when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the accordion, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [action-menu](../../packages/components/action-menu/action-menu.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The items' words, in the language of the page, and `lang` on an item in another language (3.1.2).<br>`aria-labelledby` on the `role="menu"` list pointing at the trigger, so the list has a name (4.1.2).<br>The `role="none"` on each `<li>` and `role="menuitem"` on each link or button, as the demo writes them.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover the trigger when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the menu, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [badge](../../packages/components/badge/badge.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The words, in the language of the page, and `lang` on a badge in another language (3.1.2).<br>Keeping the words short, since a badge never wraps (1.4.4, 1.4.10).<br>A busy badge that says in words what is happening ("Checking payment"), and a way to stop its motion, such as offering the quiet register (2.2.2).<br>An action for a status: the badge is never focusable, so put a button next to it.<br>The colours the page sets behind the badge, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [bloom](../../packages/components/bloom/bloom.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | A `label` in the page's language, and `lang` on it if it differs from the page (3.1.2).<br>Words that say what the count or the picture means, in the page's language, when the bloom is more than decoration.<br>The colours the page sets behind the bloom, and where it sits near deity imagery or a puja setting (see "A note on the flower"). |
| [button](../../packages/components/button/button.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The label text, in the language of the page, saying what the button does, and `lang` on a label in another language (3.1.2).<br>A link used as a button (`<a>`) is a link: put `role` and key handling on it only if the page needs a button.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a button when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the button, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [chat-thread](../../packages/components/chat-thread/chat-thread.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The messages, names and times, in the language of the page, and `lang` on a message in another language (3.1.2).<br>Redaction: removing names and numbers before the HTML is written (`renderThread`), never in the browser.<br>Keeping the quoted message on the page, since a reply quote shows only two lines of it.<br>The colours the page sets behind the thread, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [check](../../packages/components/check/check.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The label text, in the language of the page, inside the `<label>` that wraps the input, and `lang` on a label in another language (3.1.2).<br>A `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` for a group of boxes.<br>Any error text the page writes for a `required` box, next to the box (3.3.1).<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a box when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the box, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [combobox](../../packages/components/combobox/combobox.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The label, hint and error words, in the language of the page, and `lang` on an option list in another language (3.1.2).<br>The error markup: `aria-invalid` and an `aria-describedby` sentence that says what is wrong and what is valid (3.3.1).<br>The `autocomplete` token on a field that collects the reader's own details (1.3.5).<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover the input when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the input, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [connecting](../../packages/components/connecting/connecting.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The `label` text, in the language of the page, and `lang` on a label in another language (3.1.2).<br>Choosing `role="none"` only for pictures of a state, never for the one indicator that tracks a real connection.<br>A motion switch or the quiet register for the warm and playful fireflies when the state stays on screen for long (2.2.2).<br>The colours the page sets behind the element, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [data-table](../../packages/components/data-table/data-table.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The caption, the column headings and the cell text, in the language of the page, and `lang` on cells in another language (3.1.2).<br>`scope` and `headers` on a table with more than one header row or column.<br>Which columns can be sorted and the `data-value` of cells whose text is not what should sort.<br>Sticky headers or banners on the page that could cover a focused sort button or the scroll region (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the table, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [date-range](../../packages/components/date-range/date-range.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The labels of the two inputs and the legend of the fieldset, in the language of the page, and `lang` on any text in another language (3.1.2).<br>The rate card and the blocked nights the calendar draws from, and the wording of any reason a night cannot be picked.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a day when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the calendar, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [dialog](../../packages/components/dialog/dialog.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | A heading inside the dialog that is the title, or your own `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` on the `<dialog>` (4.1.2).<br>The heading, text and button words, in the language of the page, and `lang` on a passage in another language (3.1.2).<br>A motion switch or the quiet register for the animated backdrop (2.2.2).<br>Labels, instructions and errors for any form inside the dialog (3.3.1, 3.3.2).<br>A visible way to close it: the demo's Cancel button, since Escape is not available on every device.<br>The colours the page sets for the dialog's contents, if it overrides the tokens. |

The two names also hold your own words, so they carry no `lang` (3.1.2).<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a thumbnail when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>The colours the page sets behind the gallery, if it overrides the tokens. |

The Konkani words in `packages/core/strings.table.js` are a draft until a native reader checks them.<br>A sticky header or banner that could cover a link when it takes focus (2.4.11). |

The built-in words (the help line, "Undo", "Start again" and the status lines) are fixed English in `signature.core.js` with no attribute to replace them, so on a page in another language they are a passage in English: mark it with `lang` (3.1.2) or ask for them to be made replaceable.<br>`autocomplete="name"` (or the right token) on the typed-name input (1.3.5).<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover the field or a button when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>What the signature means legally, and checking a drawn signature server-side: a drawn path and a typed name are both only what the person gave. |

| [skeleton](../../packages/components/skeleton/skeleton.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | Saying in visible words that something is loading, if the skeleton is the only sign of it for sighted readers (1.4.11).<br>The `label`, so the status says what is loading ("your bookings"), in the language of the page; the built-in words ("Loading ...", "... loaded") are fixed English in `skeleton.core.js`, so on a page in another language they are a passage in English: mark it with `lang` (3.1.2) or ask for them to be made replaceable.<br>The content that replaces the skeleton, its contrast and its headings (1.4.3, 1.3.1).<br>Rendering `busy` only when a script will clear it, and not leaving it on after a failed load (a skeleton that never resolves says "Loading" for ever). |
| [sound-switch](../../packages/components/sound-switch/sound-switch.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The label text, in the language of the page, inside the `<label>` that wraps the input; `lang` on a label in another language (3.1.2).<br>The note's wording, if the page changes it.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover the switch when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>Where sound is offered at all: the switch only turns the library's cues on, and content sound (a recording, a voice) needs its own press. |
| [stamp](../../packages/components/stamp/stamp.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The words, in the language of the page: a short word and a detail line, and `lang` on a passage in another language (3.1.2). The demo carries Marathi, Kannada and Konkani stamps.<br>Rendering `pending` only when a script will land it (`stamp()`), and `role="none"` on a stamp that pictures news the page says in words elsewhere.<br>Where a playful stamp is nearly as wide as the screen, stopping the invisible halo from widening the page (for example `overflow-x: clip` on its container) until the component does it (1.4.10). |
| [stepper](../../packages/components/stepper/stepper.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The legends, labels and hints, in the language of the page, and `lang` on any in another language (3.1.2). The built-in words ("Back", "Next: ...", "Step n of N") are English in `stepper.core.js`.<br>`autocomplete` on fields that ask about the person (1.3.5), and the wording of any custom validation message (3.3.1).<br>The look of the Back and Next buttons, their focus ring and contrast (1.4.11, 2.4.7), if the page restyles them.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a field when focus moves to it (2.4.11). |
| [tabs](../../packages/components/tabs/tabs.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The label of the tablist (`aria-label` on the `<nav>`), the tab text and the panel headings, in the language of the page, and `lang` on any in another language (3.1.2). The element falls back to a name from the host when none is given.<br>Tab labels short enough to fit the narrowest width, or accepting that the row scrolls (1.4.10).<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a panel when focus moves to it (2.4.11). |
| [tile-band](../../packages/components/tile-band/tile-band.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | Whether a band is a divider (an `<hr>` inside it) or pure decoration, and keeping meaning out of it: nothing a reader needs may live only in a tile pattern.<br>Not relying on the playful tile turn to show anything; it answers a pointer or a touch and nothing else. |
| [toast](../../packages/components/toast/toast.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The words of every message, in the language of the page, short and specific, with what happened and how to fix it for an error; `lang` on a message in another language (3.1.2). The built-in words ("Notifications", "Dismiss", the tone words such as "Error") are fixed English in `toast.core.js`.<br>Making anything a person must act on an error or a toast with an action, or setting `duration="0"`, so it does not leave after its reading time (2.2.1).<br>Sticky headers and banners that sit at the top of the page when a top pile is used (2.4.11).<br>The hotkey: `Alt+Shift+T` by default, and a different `hotkey` where it clashes with the page or a screen reader. |
| [toggle](../../packages/components/toggle/toggle.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The label text: it says what the switch controls, in the language of the page, and stays inside the `<label>` that wraps the input.<br>`lang` on a label in another language (3.1.2); the demo does it for Marathi, Kannada and Konkani.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover a switch when it takes focus (2.4.11).<br>A way to turn the playful lamp's flicker off, such as offering the quiet register (2.2.2).<br>The colours the page sets behind the switch, if it overrides the tokens. |
| [tooltip](../../packages/components/tooltip/tooltip.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | Loading the script on any page where a tooltip's text is more than a hint: without it the panel cannot be dismissed with Escape (1.4.13).<br>The trigger: a real `<button>` or link with its own name, and the tooltip's words, in the language of the page, and `lang` on a tooltip in another language (3.1.2).<br>Never putting a meaning someone must act on (a price, a deadline) only in a tooltip: say it in real text nearby too.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover the trigger when it takes focus (2.4.11). |
| [tumble](../../packages/components/tumble/tumble.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The heading's text, in the language of the page, and its colour and ground: at least 4.5:1 for text (1.4.3), or 3:1 for large text.<br>A real heading element (`<h1>` to `<h6>` or `role="heading"`) inside the element, and a sensible heading order for the page.<br>`hold` only where a script will play the heading; a held heading is hidden until it plays, and is given back after 8 seconds if nobody plays it. |
| [voice-note](../../packages/components/voice-note/voice-note.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The transcript: a `.sg-voice-transcript` element with the words that are said, in the language of the audio, and `lang` on it when that differs from the page (1.2.1, 3.1.2).<br>The note's `label`, so the button says which note it plays ("Play voice message, from Maya").<br>The built-in words ("Play voice message", "Pause voice message", "Position in the voice message", "of") are fixed English in `voice-note.core.js`; on a page in another language they are a passage in English: mark it with `lang` (3.1.2) or ask for them to be made replaceable.<br>Sticky headers and banners that could cover the note when it takes focus (2.4.11). |
| [wa-order](../../packages/components/wa-order/wa-order.docs.md#conformance-wcag-22-aa) | The words the page gives: `business`, `areas`, `slots`, the menu it reads, and the number, in the language of the page; the element's own labels, hints and messages ("Day you want it", "Pick the day you want it.", "Send on WhatsApp") are fixed English in `wa-order.core.js`, so on a page in another language they are a passage in English: mark it with `lang` (3.1.2) or ask for them to be made replaceable.<br>Sticky bars and banners that could cover a field when it takes focus, such as a total bar from the menu (2.4.11).<br>Saying, near the link, that it opens WhatsApp in a new tab, if the audit wants it (3.2.5 is level AAA).<br>What happens after the person sends the message: the library writes the order and hands it over, and never says it is placed. |

## GIGW 3.0

GIGW 3.0 asks for conformance with WCAG 2.1 level AA for accessibility (the secondary sources we read say so, and also name IS 17802). WCAG 2.2 level AA adds six criteria at levels A and AA and removes 4.1.1, so a table written to 2.2 AA covers 2.1 AA. The mapping from GIGW checkpoints to WCAG criteria is in `docs/contributing/conformance.md`, with what we could and could not verify against the guideline text.
